position_outside: UN/LOCODE places Adabiya at (29.8667, 32.4667), on land by a quarry about 600 m from the Suez to Ain Sokhna road, about 4.4 km south of the port area.

properties.source: Derived: the convex hull of this port's terminals from OpenStreetMap, grown by 300 m, then cut to the water OpenStreetMap maps inside it (the sea within its coastline, rivers, docks and basins), with the terminals kept whole
properties.note: OpenStreetMap maps no port limits for Adabiya. These are the hull of the Adabiya port area grown by 300 m, cut to the water OpenStreetMap maps inside it, with the port area kept whole: the quays and the water off them. The two C1 anchorages lie outside, 2.4 to 2.8 km south-south-east. A scan of OpenStreetMap finds no homes, residential land, schools, hospitals, places of worship or named places inside. Two neighbourhood outlines in OpenStreetMap take in the port area and some of its water: Al Attaka and one with no name.

properties.name: C1
properties.note: Seamark anchorage off Adabiya, named C1 in OpenStreetMap, which gives it no category. The farther of the two C1 areas from the port, south-south-east of its quays.

properties.name: ميناء الأدبية
properties.note: The port area, mapped as industrial land named ميناء الأدبية (Adabiya Port) in OpenStreetMap, which gives it no English name. SCZONE, which manages the port, lists eight berths, 1,465 m in all, for dry and liquid bulk, general and project cargo, containers and livestock, and names no single operator for them. OpenStreetMap's area, about 26 ha, is smaller than the 114 ha SCZONE gives for the port.
